input.prompt: The camera itself is completely locked off and motionless like a tripod photograph, with absolutely no zoom, no push-in, no drift, no pan and no camera movement of any kind for the entire clip. The framed 'NO WINE, NO LIFE.' pop-art poster on the wall (a hand holding a glass of red wine on a bright yellow background) stays perfectly rigid, flat and exactly the same size for the entire clip: its illustration, hand, glass, lettering, ALCOHOLIDAY logo, white border and proportions never warp, stretch, resize, shift position or change perspective, as if it truly is a static print and not a generated image. The only motion anywhere in this shot is the leaves of the small potted plant on the desk: they sway very gently as if touched by a soft breeze; every leaf stays firmly attached. Everything else in the room, including the furniture, the desk and everything on it, the shelves, the books, the bags, the clothes, the bed and especially the framed poster, is completely still and motionless. A quiet night in the small tidy one-room apartment of a 23-year-old office worker, warm desk lamp light inside and city lights outside. No steam, no smoke, no haze. No people. All motion is small, slow and calm.
